newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Passenger ship adrift in Pacific, rescue underway.
newsitem.headline: Passenger ship adrift in Pacific, rescue underway.

text.p: A charter ship with 290 passengers was adrift in the central Pacific without power on Wednesday after a fire in its engine room, Australian maritime officials said.

The 64.5-metre (210 foot) Maasmond was en-route from the Kiribati island of Tarawa to Christmas Island when a fire in its engine room crippled the ship late on Tuesday and forced it to appeal for help, Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray told Reuters.
"The radio message said an engine room and switchboard fire had left the vessel without power and that it was requesting assistance," Gray said.

He said a Royal New Zealand Air Force search plane and a Royal New Zealand Navy patrol boat had been dispatched to help the boat, which was drifting about 800 kms (500 miles) east of Tarawa in Kiribati, a group of coral atolls about 5,000 kms (3,000 miles) north-east of Sydney.
Gray said it was not clear from the distress message if the fire was out, but that the ship had requested a tow.
New Zealand Air Force officials were not immediately available for comment on the distressed ship.
The MV Maasmond is registered in Kingstown in St Vincent and Grenadines, according to the Lloyds List, and has had engine trouble in the past.
In 1992, it underwent engine repairs for ten weeks after encountering cyclones on a cruise through the Pacific.
